strategy.title: Follow-Through Day (FTD)
strategy.text: Qualification Requirements A valid Follow-Through Day requires a gain of 1.0% or greater on higher volume than the prior session on either the NASDAQ Composite or S&P 500, occurring on Day 4 or later of an official rally attempt.

strategy.title: Tentative Nature of Early Signals
strategy.text: Should a Follow-Through Day materialize during Friday's shortened session or early next week, investors must treat it as an initial signal to deploy pilot capital ("dip the toe in the water") rather than an aggressive "all-in" buy regime.

strategy.title: Technical Quality Constraints
strategy.text: An FTD generated below key moving average lines (such as the 200-day SMA or 21-day EMA) or beneath prior pivot lows carries a higher failure rate than a breakout out of a power base.

strategy.title: Risk Guardrails
strategy.text: The absolute low of the Follow-Through Day session serves as the immediate stop-loss line in the sand. A close below the FTD low invalidates the rally attempt and mandates an immediate return to cash. Portfolio Exposure & Volatility-Adjusted Position Sizing In high-ATR market environments (where individual growth stocks feature 7% to 10% daily price swings), traditional position sizing must be scaled back significantly: 1. Pilot Sizing: Limit initial position sizes to 2% to 3% of total portfolio capital (or half-positions) to prevent capital erosion during intraday whipsaws. 2. ATR-Based Stop Placement: Account for wider stock-specific volatility bands (e.g., JROG's 9.5% ATR) by setting logical stop losses beneath weekly moving average support rather than tight intraday stops that invite shakeouts. 3. Patience for Base Maturation: Focus exclusively on equities maintaining RS lines near high ground (such as CHYM, CDNA, and JROG), allowing V-shaped intraday swings to settle into proper, multi-week consolidation patterns before expanding exposure.

sections.title: Follow-Through Day Mechanics, ATR-Calibrated Sizing, and Risk Execution Rules

items.text: Navigating a market locked in a rally attempt within a broader downtrend requires strict adherence to institutional risk protocols. Aggressive capital deployment prior to structural market confirmation exposes portfolios to severe whipsaw losses.

items.title: Follow-Through Day (FTD)
items.text: Qualification Requirements A valid Follow-Through Day requires a gain of 1.0% or greater on higher volume than the prior session on either the NASDAQ Composite or S&P 500, occurring on Day 4 or later of an official rally attempt.

items.title: Tentative Nature of Early Signals
items.text: Should a Follow-Through Day materialize during Friday's shortened session or early next week, investors must treat it as an initial signal to deploy pilot capital ("dip the toe in the water") rather than an aggressive "all-in" buy regime.

items.title: Technical Quality Constraints
items.text: An FTD generated below key moving average lines (such as the 200-day SMA or 21-day EMA) or beneath prior pivot lows carries a higher failure rate than a breakout out of a power base.

items.title: Risk Guardrails
items.text: The absolute low of the Follow-Through Day session serves as the immediate stop-loss line in the sand. A close below the FTD low invalidates the rally attempt and mandates an immediate return to cash. Portfolio Exposure & Volatility-Adjusted Position Sizing In high-ATR market environments (where individual growth stocks feature 7% to 10% daily price swings), traditional position sizing must be scaled back significantly: 1. Pilot Sizing: Limit initial position sizes to 2% to 3% of total portfolio capital (or half-positions) to prevent capital erosion during intraday whipsaws. 2. ATR-Based Stop Placement: Account for wider stock-specific volatility bands (e.g., JROG's 9.5% ATR) by setting logical stop losses beneath weekly moving average support rather than tight intraday stops that invite shakeouts. 3. Patience for Base Maturation: Focus exclusively on equities maintaining RS lines near high ground (such as CHYM, CDNA, and JROG), allowing V-shaped intraday swings to settle into proper, multi-week consolidation patterns before expanding exposure.
